artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite group of order $g$. For $w \in G$, define
$$f(w) = \#\{(u,v) \in G \times G : w = uvu^{-1}v^{-1}\}.$$
Then $f$ is a class function on $G$, and its expansion in terms of the irreducible complex characters of $G$ is
$$f = \sum_{\chi \in \mathrm{Irr}(G)} \frac{g}{\chi(1)}\, \chi,$$
where the sum runs over all irreducible characters $\chi$ of $G$. In particular, $f$ is a (nonnegative integer combination) character of $G$, which forces $\chi(1) \mid g$ for each irreducible character $\chi$.

Construct an explicit (combinatorially or algebraically described) finite-dimensional complex $G$-module $M$ whose character equals $f$. The construction must be explicit enough that:
(i) it directly exhibits $f$ as a real (in fact ordinary) character of $G$, and
(ii) since the irreducible characters $\chi$ are linearly independent, comparing the character of $M$ with $\sum_\chi \frac{g}{\chi(1)}\chi$ yields a new, representation-theoretic proof that $\chi(1)$ divides $|G|$ for every irreducible character $\chi$ of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known open problem (Stanley, Enumerative Combinatorics vol. 2, Exercise 7.68(b)): although the formula for the commutator-counting class function as a sum over irreducible characters is classical, no explicit combinatorial/representation-theoretic construction of a $G$-module realizing this character is known, and such a construction would yield a new proof that $\chi(1)$ divides $|G|$. Web search did not turn up a published solution.

status_evidence.snippet: Exercise 7.68(b) asks for an explicit G-module whose character is the commutator-counting function f(w)=#{(u,v): w=uvu^{-1}v^{-1}}.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of finding such an explicit module is listed as an open problem.
